cross_sector_overview: Across health, aged care, NDIS, child protection and early learning, funding pressure and contested reform design (the stalled private health insurance rebate cut, NDIS reassessments and Thriving Kids, inquiry-driven child safety reform, childcare viability) are colliding with workforce strain and Commonwealth-state responsibility gaps. That points to PEPI demand for modelling, system and market-stewardship design, implementation and transition support, and cost and workforce analysis, with AI and data-centre infrastructure emerging as a cross-cutting policy and market theme.

pepi_wide.brief: Fiscal and system-capacity pressure dominated the week across the PEPI portfolio. The private health insurance rebate cut is stalled in the Senate: the Greens and Coalition object to the pensioner carve-out, and departmental modelling shows about 80,000 older Australians dropping cover. That leaves the budget-repair path uncertain and adds hospital cost risk. Aged care reform is straining under Support at Home and residential fee changes, a waitlist backlog above 100,000 with rising waitlist deaths, and peak-body objections to the 2.55% AN-ACC increase. NDIS reassessments, Thriving Kids transitions and provider registration are moving fast with little clarity. Child protection inquiries in WA, Queensland and South Australia, and early learning and homelessness pressures, point to state-led reform and evaluation demand. Advisory opportunities sit in rebate and concession modelling, package supply and demand forecasting, Commonwealth-state transition design, regulatory design and hospital-to-community pathway reform. Watch for Budget measures and consultation-driven procurement, including NDIS registration, Support at Home evaluation and assessment services.

synthesis.brief: Child protection is under acute pressure in WA and Queensland: a WA child safety crisis with Elders calling for a royal commission and a Commissioner's Pilbara probe, a Commonwealth-state blame shift over Indigenous child safety, and a Queensland minister claiming the system has 'stabilised' despite fewer urgent cases seen on time. A South Australian inquiry finding a 'cliff edge' for care leavers, reunification model criticism and Queensland's $1.7m spend on three foster carers point to demand for system review, placement and cost-model redesign, and leaving-care and transition support (including NDIS interface). Expect inquiry-driven reform, Closing the Gap accountability pressure and advisory or evaluation opportunities for PEPI.
